ColonyCouncil.AlmanacArticleDef.label: the gods on the map
ColonyCouncil.AlmanacArticleDef.summary: A few times in a long game a god comes to the colony itself: as a stranger at the gate, as a beast like no other, or only in the sky. Omens come first, and what it leaves is remembered for years.
ColonyCouncil.AlmanacArticleDef.tip: Treat strangers at the gate well. Leave a beast that glows alone, or take it food, or follow it when it looks back at you.
ColonyCouncil.AlmanacArticleDef.description: The gods don't only live on the Gods page. Now and then one comes to the colony, after days of signs, and how the colony treats it decides what it leaves behind. Who comes as what is each god's own: not every god has a body, not every one with a body has a beast, and some show only in the weather. How real the gods are decides how plainly it happens: in Walking a god shows itself and speaks, in Felt it's gone before anyone can be sure and some say, and in Believed no god comes at all, though the colony still reads its gods into the weather.

li.heading: The omens
li.text: In the days before a god comes, one sign a day: every bird on the land leaving at once, a strange calm with the wind dead and nothing moving, two colonists waking from the same dream, a lamp or torch that won't stay lit, the animals restless and all looking one way. Someone who saw it says so, and the news says whose sign it was. Nothing ever says when the god will come.

points.li: A lone traveller of the colony's age (a wanderer, a pilgrim, a drifter, a lost spacer) asks for shelter. Give them a bed and a place at the table, let them sleep by the gate (what happens if nobody answers), or turn them away.
Let in, they are Hospitality's guest when it is loaded, with its guest beds and table; otherwise they sleep in a warm corner indoors. Whoever answered the gate goes to talk with them that evening.

They are a god in disguise, and it shows to those who look: animals follow them, no footprints in the snow, a shimmer about them at night. They say things a traveller couldn't know, and thank the cook by name after a good meal.

They notice everything: the bed they got, what they ate, who talked with them, who shared a meal or a drink, gave them something or tended their wounds, how the animals are kept, and whether anyone strikes or robs them.

li.heading: When the stranger goes

table.li: How they were kept | What comes of it
Struck or robbed | The god shows itself at once in anger, and is gone. Its domain is withheld for a while, and whoever struck it may come down with a fever
Turned away | The god shows itself on the road (in Walking) or is simply gone. Its domain is withheld for a while
Poorly | The god is displeased, and leaves nothing
Fairly | The god is pleased, and something is found where it stood
Kindly, or like family | A find, rain where the god brings rain, and the kindest colonist gets a lasting gift

li.after: The kindest colonist's gift is of the god's domain: a burning passion for its work, a trait, with A RimWorld of Magic a spell scroll (for one who casts) or a class, or the god's favour and a spark of inspiration. A withheld domain is the rain kept from the fields for some days, dry thunder over the colony, the wild game leaving the land, or the colony's lights guttering for a night. The fever is held to the same cap and illness budget as every hurt from everyday life.

points.li: A god walks as a beast of its own, larger than its kind and lit from within, the player's mods' beasts first. It comes in from the edge, stays a few days and goes. It can't be tamed, and it is never hostile unless harmed.
A small one (a crow, a cat, an otter) follows one colonist about. A large one walks the land, and may come to someone out of doors and wait for them to follow.
Right-click it with a colonist: follow it where it leads, or take it food from the stores. It leads to a find, a cure for what ails the one who follows, or a seam of ore nobody had seen.

Leaving it be pleases its god, feeding and following it more. Hunting or hurting it is sacrilege: the game's own revenge, the sky darkening in the god's anger, a fever perhaps on whoever did it, and a slain one's body goes to ash.

li.heading: Weather as a voice

table.li: The harvest's or the waters', pleased | Rain, if the land has rain now
A god of storms, either way | Thunder on cue, and the land's storm
A dark god (the dead, the night, the void), angered, by day | An eclipse
A god of the night, the road or the dead, pleased, at night | An aurora

li.after: Only after the colony's deeds move a god it knows, by a chance by how loudly that god answers, as the land and the game's own rules allow, and some days apart. A god with no body acts this way most of all. Someone out of doors always names it. In Believed nothing is sent: the weather that comes of itself after a deed is what the colony reads as the answer.

li.heading: What remains
li.text: The god's act goes on its page and in the colony's chronicle and history. Those who saw it share the memory and bring it up when they talk, and the kindest, the one who followed, the one who fed it and whoever struck a god are talked about. The mark it left on the land is remembered for years: someone walks out to it on a quiet day and stands there remembering aloud, someone at supper brings it up, and visitors who pass it ask about it.

li.heading: This week
li.text: Under way lists a stranger at the gate or staying, and a beast on the land. Nothing that is coming is ever listed: only the omens say so.
